Based on overall experimental observations, especially the pair processes, I developed a model structure of the vacuum along with a basic-particle formation scheme begun in 2000 (with collaborator P-I Johansson). The model consists in that the vacuum is, briefly, filled of neutral but polarizable vacuuons, consisting each of a p-vaculeon and n- vaculeon of charges $+e$ and $-e$ of zero rest masses but with spin motions, assumed interacting each other with a Coulomb force. The model has been introduced in full in a book (Nova Sci, 2005) and referred to in a number of journal/E-print papers. I outline in this easier accessible paper the detailed derivation of the model and a corresponding quantitative determination of the vacuuon size.

Beginning in 2000, the author, together with collaborator P.-I. Johansson, developed a model for the structure of the vacuum and a corresponding scheme for the formation of basic particles. This approach was intended to provide a conceptual framework in which the vacuum is not treated as empty space, but rather as a medium with an internal structure.

In this model, the vacuum is proposed to be filled with neutral yet polarizable entities called “vacuuons.” Although each vacuuon has no net electric charge, it is assumed to be capable of polarization under suitable conditions. This polarizability arises from its internal composition.

A vacuuon is described as being made up of two constituent components: a positively charged “p-vaculeon” and a negatively charged “n-vaculeon.” The p-vaculeon carries a charge of \(+e\), while the n-vaculeon carries a charge of \(-e\). Both constituents are assumed to have zero rest mass and to possess spin motions. Together, these two oppositely charged components form a neutral composite object.

The interaction between the p-vaculeon and the n-vaculeon is assumed to be governed by the Coulomb force. Because the two components carry equal and opposite charges, they attract each other electrically, and this attraction is taken to play a central role in the structure and stability of the vacuuon.

The paper presents the derivation of this vacuum-structure model and describes how it leads to a proposed scheme for the formation of basic particles. In addition, it provides a quantitative determination of the size of the vacuuon, offering a numerical estimate for this fundamental unit within the proposed vacuum model.
outputs.L4:
This text presents a proposed model of vacuum structure and a related scheme for the formation of basic particles. The model is developed from experimental observations of pair processes, especially processes in which particle–antiparticle pairs appear to emerge from interactions involving radiation and the vacuum. On this basis, the vacuum is not treated as empty space, but as a structured medium composed of elementary neutral units called “vacuuons.”

In the proposed picture, each vacuuon is electrically neutral as a whole, but it is made up of two oppositely charged components. These components are assumed to have zero rest mass and to interact with one another through the Coulomb force. Because the positive and negative constituents can be displaced relative to one another, a vacuuon is polarizable. The vacuum therefore behaves as a medium that can respond to electromagnetic disturbances, while still remaining neutral on average.

The model connects this vacuum structure to the formation of basic particles. According to the proposed scheme, particles may arise from particular configurations or excitations of the vacuum’s charged constituents. Pair formation processes are interpreted as evidence that the vacuum contains the necessary charged substructure from which matter–antimatter pairs can be produced under suitable conditions. In this way, the model attempts to give a physical mechanism for particle creation rather than treating it only as an abstract quantum process.

The full formulation of this vacuum model and particle-formation scheme has been presented previously. The present text aims to give a more accessible derivation of the same ideas, emphasizing the physical reasoning behind the model and clarifying the assumptions on which it is based. A central part of this discussion is the quantitative determination of the size of the vacuuon. By estimating this characteristic size, the model seeks to assign a definite scale to the proposed vacuum structure.

The determined vacuuon size is presented as significant because it provides a concrete parameter for describing the vacuum as a polarizable medium. It also serves as a basis for understanding how electromagnetic interactions, vacuum polarization, and particle formation might be related within the same framework. Thus, the text argues that identifying the size and properties of the vacuuon may help provide a deeper physical interpretation of both the vacuum and the origin of basic particles.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract in a non-native academic style describing a speculative vacuum model involving polarizable neutral vacuuons made of charged p- and n-vaculeons, referencing work begun in 2000 with P-I Johansson and a 2005 Nova Science book.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

In this paper is presented a speculative model of physical vacuum, originally developed in work started in year 2000 together with P-I Johansson and later described in the 2005 Nova Science Publishers book. The vacuum is assumed not to be an empty geometrical background, but a polarizable medium composed of neutral elementary entities, here called *vacuuons*. Each vacuuon is considered as a bound structure made from two oppositely charged constituents, denoted as positive and negative *vaculeons* or p- and n-vaculeons. Although the vacuuon is electrically neutral in its undisturbed state, it may become polarized under influence of charges, fields, or matter particles. In this way the ordinary electromagnetic field is interpreted as a macroscopic manifestation of microscopic polarization processes inside the vacuum medium.

The model gives a possible phenomenological picture where electric permittivity, magnetic permeability, and propagation of light are connected with collective response of the vacuuon structure. Matter particles may be treated as special local excitations or deformations of this vacuum substance, and forces can be understood as resulting from gradients and rearrangements of polarization. Such approach is not intended as a replacement of established quantum electrodynamics, but as an alternative conceptual framework for discussing the origin of field properties and vacuum constants. The theory remains highly speculative and requires further mathematical formulation and experimental consequences. Nevertheless, it may offer intuitive possibilities for connecting electromagnetism, inertia, and vacuum structure in one common physical model.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a brief first-person overview for an easier accessible physics article about a vacuum model motivated by experimental observations of pair processes, including its publication history and the derivation of vacuuon size.
counterfactuals.output:
I wrote this article to give a non-specialist account of a speculative vacuum model that was inspired by familiar experimental facts: photons can create electron–positron pairs near matter, and electron–positron pairs can annihilate back into photons. These pair processes suggest a way to picture the vacuum not as empty space, but as a medium with a hidden microscopic structure. In the model I describe, the basic element of that structure is called a **vacuuon**—an idealized, neutral unit associated with a virtual particle–antiparticle pair.

The idea was first developed in manuscript/preprint form and later revised into a more accessible article so that the assumptions, physical motivation, and limitations could be seen clearly. I emphasize that the vacuuon picture is not part of standard quantum electrodynamics, but an interpretive model motivated by observed pair creation and annihilation phenomena.

A simple estimate of the vacuuon size comes from the energy needed to create an electron–positron pair. The threshold energy is

\[
E = 2m_ec^2 ,
\]

where \(m_e\) is the electron mass. Associating this energy with a photon through

\[
E = \frac{hc}{\lambda},
\]

gives

\[
\lambda = \frac{h}{2m_ec}.
\]

This is one half of the electron Compton wavelength:

\[
\lambda \approx 1.21 \times 10^{-12}\ \text{m}.
\]

In the article, I use this length as the natural scale for the vacuuon: the approximate distance over which the vacuum unit is associated with the energy of an electron–positron pair. This derivation is not meant as a proof of the model, but as an accessible way to connect the proposed vacuum structure with measurable pair-production physics.
